output.brief: The wrong dates were not caused by the agency operators or the printer firmware. The printer records show that from 4 Oct the data sent to the printers already carried a 36-month shelf life. No operator overrode anything, and the camera passed every carton because it only checks the print against the job. The same wrong value reached Line 1 day shift, run by permanent staff. Firmware 4.3 had been running for days with correct dates. The ERP history shows Regulatory Affairs entered 36 months on 3 Oct, but it is only meant to apply from March 2027. The current value is still 24. The integration service evidently picked up the future-dated value, despite the vendor's claim that it can't. That is the likely cause, and the vendor and IT should explain how it happened. Cancel the warnings and the removal of the agency operators. Reset the Veltranol record and extend the hold to all Veltranol lots since 4 Oct, including the two in the warehouse. Add a second-person check of printed expiry against the batch record at each setup. Inspect other products with future-dated edits, HX-15-30 and MR-05-14. Keep the camera check running. I'm fairly confident about Veltranol. Other products are unconfirmed. A full 12-month reconciliation and over-labelling of other stock are not justified yet.
